correctness.rationale: For arbitrary nonzero real vectors, the full norming-functional family of ell-one gives the signed-support criterion. Axis support forces the remaining clique into an ell-one plane with maximum two. Two members of each two-coordinate support must be the two precise diagonals. Two distinct full-support sign functionals force a zero coordinate in a common kernel, so at most two full-support members; a full-support member allows at most one line for each two-coordinate support and hence at most five in all. Three support pairs times two gives six; all six constructed diagonals satisfy mutual equations, and equality forces exactly their six projective lines. The independent piecewise-linear criterion agrees with the support criterion on 2466 rational-grid ordered pairs, with exactly one maximum clique on the 49-line dimension-three grid; these are finite checks, not the proof.

value.rationale: Exact projective mutual Birkhoff--James clique number is an intrinsic Banach-space graph invariant explicitly motivated by 2021 norm-dependent clique questions and 2023 examples. Its sharp six-line threshold and full equality-case rigidity, rather than an arbitrary bounded-coordinate enumeration, quantify the first dimension-three coordinate-support competition in classical nonsmooth ell-one geometry. The fact is not a mere reformulation of the two-dimensional pair classification: three support strata and exclusion of full-support vectors are essential. A precise extremal model can be used as a benchmark in higher-dimensional orthograph questions, without claiming it solves those questions.
